title: Let SDK users set the file allowlists

labels.name: community
labels.description: PRs from the community. This label is used to ensure all community PRs get reviewed.

body:
Thank you for submitting this pull request. We really appreciate you spending the time to work on SurrealDB. 🚀 🎉

<!-- Before proceeding, please add any of the following labels that apply:

* `breaking-change` if this PR includes a breaking change. This label is not needed for bug fixes, which change output in line with a user's original expectations.
* `needs-documentation` if documentation is needed to explain the change made in the PR.
* `Modifies env vars or commands` if any changes are made to environment variables or command flags. -->

> Stacked on #7556, #7558 and #7560. Until they merge, review only the last commit, "Let SDK users set the file allowlists".

## What is the motivation?

<!-- Please provide details on the motivation for why you have made this change.-->

The SDK's embedded engines never pass the bucket folder or file allowlists to the datastore, and `opt::Config` has no setters for them. An empty allowlist denies every path, so from the embedded SDK, natively and in the browser:

- `file://` buckets are unusable (#7353);
- analyzer mapper files (`DEFINE ANALYZER ... FILTERS mapper('...')`) are always denied.

## What does this change do?

<!-- Please provide a description of what this pull request does, and how it solves the problem. -->

- Adds two setters to the SDK's `Config`:
  - `bucket_folder_allowlist(paths)`: the folders `file://` buckets may use. In the browser, these are OPFS paths.
  - `file_allowlist(paths)`: the folders local files, such as analyzer mappers, may be read from.
- The native and browser engines hand both to the new `DatastoreBuilder::with_bucket_folder_allowlist` and `DatastoreBuilder::with_file_allowlist`. When set, each replaces the matching `ConfigMap` value. When not set, nothing changes.
- Paths go through as `PathBuf`s, with no joining and re-splitting on a platform delimiter. They are cleaned, and file allowlist paths canonicalized, by the same code the string settings use.

Thanks to @efortin, whose #7352 found both gaps. This PR builds on it and:

- wires the browser engine too, which #7560 needs for SDK users;
- passes typed paths through the datastore builder instead of a delimiter-joined `ConfigMap` string, so paths containing `:` or `;` and non-UTF-8 paths survive.

## What is your testing strategy?

<!-- Write your test plan here. Please provide us with clear instructions on how you verified your changes work. -->

In `surrealdb/tests/api_integration` (`cargo make ci-api-integration-mem`):

- `file_buckets_need_an_allowed_folder` defines a `file://` bucket in a temporary folder. Without the allowlist the script is denied; with the folder allowed, a file written to the bucket is read back.
- `analyzer_mappers_need_an_allowed_folder` defines an analyzer with a mapper file from a temporary folder. Without the allowlist the definition is denied; with the folder allowed, `search::analyze` applies the mapping.

In the browser, `file_buckets_use_allowed_folders` in `surrealdb/web-tests/tests/sdk.rs` checks buckets through the SDK in headless Chrome (`cargo make ci-web-test`). The browser has no local files to map, so mappers are covered natively only.

Each test fails when the engines don't forward the allowlist. The browser test helpers now go through the new builder method instead of a `ConfigMap`, so the other file bucket tests exercise it too.

## Security Considerations

<!-- Briefly assess the security implications of this change. Consider:
- Does it touch authentication, authorization, or session handling?
- Does it affect data isolation between namespaces or databases?
- Does it process user input that reaches the query engine or storage layer?
- Could error messages or logs expose internal details?
- Are resource limits enforced for any new user-controlled operations?

See SECURITY_GUIDE.md for the security invariants reviewers will check.

If there are no security implications, briefly state why (e.g. "documentation-only change").
If there are security implications, or you're uncertain, please assign the `security-review` label to this PR
and request a security review by a member of the @surrealdb/security team. -->

This widens what an embedder can allow, never what a query can reach on its own. Access stays denied unless the embedding application opts in:

- both allowlists default to empty;
- file buckets also need the experimental `files` capability.

Allowed paths are prepared by the same code as the string settings, and requested paths are still canonicalized and prefix-checked, so `..` and symlinks cannot escape an allowed folder. The server keeps reading `SURREAL_BUCKET_FOLDER_ALLOWLIST` and `SURREAL_FILE_ALLOWLIST` as before.

## Is this related to any issues?

<!-- If this pull request is related to other pull requests, or resolves any issues, then link all related or closed items here, using 'Closes #101' or 'Fixes #101' to automatically close any linked issues. -->

Fixes #7353

- Supersedes #7352, see above.
- Related: #6776 asks for a non-environment way to set the allowlist for embedders.

<!-- All pull requests require that the contributing guidelines have been read and agreed to. -->

title: Support files in the browser

labels.name: community
labels.description: PRs from the community. This label is used to ensure all community PRs get reviewed.

body:
Thank you for submitting this pull request. We really appreciate you spending the time to work on SurrealDB. 🚀 🎉

<!-- Before proceeding, please add any of the following labels that apply:

* `breaking-change` if this PR includes a breaking change. This label is not needed for bug fixes, which change output in line with a user's original expectations.
* `needs-documentation` if documentation is needed to explain the change made in the PR.
* `Modifies env vars or commands` if any changes are made to environment variables or command flags. -->

> Stacked on #7556 and #7558. Until they merge, review only the last commit, "Support files in the browser".

## What is the motivation?

<!-- Please provide details on the motivation for why you have made this change.-->

File buckets are unavailable in the browser: `DEFINE BUCKET ... BACKEND "file://..."` on `wasm32-unknown-unknown` fails with "Bucket backend is not supported" (#7559). Offline-first web apps on the embedded engine have nowhere to keep files.

The browser engine also ignored `Config::capabilities`, so the experimental `files` feature could not be allowed there, and denies such as `with_function_denied` were silently dropped.

## What does this change do?

<!-- Please provide a description of what this pull request does, and how it solves the problem. -->

- **OPFS-backed file buckets.** With tokio aliased to `tokio_with_wasm` in the browser (#7556), `tokio::fs` there is backed by the origin private file system. A `file_buckets` cfg from `build.rs` turns file buckets on natively and in the browser. WASI and other wasm targets have no tokio `fs` and keep them off.
- **Capabilities.** The browser engine passes the configured capabilities to the datastore, as the native engine does.
- **`Send`.** OPFS futures hold JS handles and are not `Send`. The browser runs on one thread, so there the `ObjectStore` and connect futures drop the `Send` bound, the way transaction builders already do on wasm. Store methods name their future through a `StoreFuture` alias, so the bound changes in one place, and `memory.rs` and `prefixed.rs` get shorter.
- **Rename.** OPFS has no move, so a browser rename copies, then removes the source. Renaming a file onto itself is a no-op instead of deleting it, and if the source cannot be removed, the target is restored.
- **Paths and times.** std treats no path as absolute in the browser, so the bucket root is checked with `has_root` there. Modification times fall back to chrono's clock, since `web_time`'s `SystemTime` is not std's on the web.

What this improves:

- `file://` buckets and the `file::*` functions work in the browser, and files persist across sessions in OPFS.
- Browser capabilities behave as configured, including denies.
- `FileStore` behaves the same on both targets, and native tests now cover every operation.

## What is your testing strategy?

<!-- Write your test plan here. Please provide us with clear instructions on how you verified your changes work. -->

Browser, in headless Chrome (`cargo make ci-web-test`):

- `file_buckets.rs`: put, get, head, delete, put-if-not-exists, copy, rename, rename onto itself, list with filters and pagination, persistence across datastores, keys escaping the root, roots outside the allowlist, and a file as the root.
- `file_buckets_locked.rs`: runs in a dedicated worker, which holds a file open with a sync access handle so it cannot be removed. It checks that a failed rename restores a replaced target and removes a newly created one.
- `sdk.rs`: `capabilities_apply` denies `string::len` through `Config::capabilities` and expects the query to be refused.

Written before the fix, these fail with "Bucket backend is not supported". With OPFS enabled but without the copy-then-remove rename, the rename-onto-itself and locked-file tests fail. Switching `has_root` back to `is_absolute` rejects every root as "not absolute".

Native: new `FileStore` tests in `buc/store/file.rs` cover every operation, the escaping-key checks, `head` metadata and root validation. Run with `cargo test -p surrealdb-core buc`.

## Security Considerations

<!-- Briefly assess the security implications of this change. Consider:
- Does it touch authentication, authorization, or session handling?
- Does it affect data isolation between namespaces or databases?
- Does it process user input that reaches the query engine or storage layer?
- Could error messages or logs expose internal details?
- Are resource limits enforced for any new user-controlled operations?

See SECURITY_GUIDE.md for the security invariants reviewers will check.

If there are no security implications, briefly state why (e.g. "documentation-only change").
If there are security implications, or you're uncertain, please assign the `security-review` label to this PR
and request a security review by a member of the @surrealdb/security team. -->

- **Capabilities.** Browser capabilities now come from the SDK config. Users who set none get the same defaults as before. Users who set some now get exactly what they asked for: denies take effect, and allows (for example the `files` feature or network targets) are no longer ignored.
- **Paths.** File buckets stay behind the experimental `files` capability and the bucket folder allowlist, which default to off and empty. Keys that escape the bucket root are rejected on both targets, and the tests cover it. In the browser all paths live in the origin's own OPFS, which other origins cannot reach.

Could a maintainer add the `security-review` label?

## Is this related to any issues?

<!-- If this pull request is related to other pull requests, or resolves any issues, then link all related or closed items here, using 'Closes #101' or 'Fixes #101' to automatically close any linked issues. -->

Fixes #7559

- Requested in surrealdb/suggestions#9 and surrealdb/surrealdb.js#548.
- SDK users still cannot allow bucket folders; that is #7353, fixed by #7561.

## Have you read the Contributing Guidelines?

<!-- All pull requests require that the contributing guidelines have been read and agreed to. -->

* [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

title: Support file buckets in the browser, backed by OPFS

labels.name: topic:rust
labels.description: This is related to the Rust embedded library

labels.name: sdk-issue
labels.description: Issues with the Rust SDK specifically

type.name: Feature
type.description: A feature request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### What component does this affect?

SurrealDB Rust SDK

### Is this feature related to a problem?

File buckets (`DEFINE BUCKET ... BACKEND "file://..."`) are unavailable in the browser: defining one on `wasm32-unknown-unknown` fails with "Bucket backend is not supported". Offline-first web apps using the embedded engine (for example over IndexedDB) have nowhere to keep files, and fall back to storing blobs in records or to a remote server.

The browser engine also ignores `Config::capabilities`, so the experimental `files` feature cannot be allowed there. For the same reason, denies such as `with_function_denied` are silently dropped.

Requested before in surrealdb/suggestions#9 and surrealdb/surrealdb.js#548, where opening a feature request here was suggested.

### Suggest a solution

Back `file://` buckets with the origin private file system (OPFS), which every current browser provides per origin.

- Once tokio is aliased to `tokio_with_wasm` in the browser (#7556), `tokio::fs` there is OPFS-backed, so the existing `FileStore` can compile for the browser with few changes.
- Where OPFS differs from a real file system: it has no rename, so a move copies then removes; its futures are not `Send`; and std treats no path as absolute there, so bucket roots are checked with `has_root`.
- Forward the configured capabilities to the browser datastore, as the native engine does.

Allowing bucket folders from the SDK is tracked separately in #7353.

### Alternative methods

Storing file contents as bytes in records, which bloats the key-value store and loses the file API, or using a remote SurrealDB server, which rules out offline use.

### SurrealDB version

surrealdb 3.3.0-nightly (main at 18971ffb), wasm32-unknown-unknown

title: Storing an ML model in the browser panics: "current directory should be accessible"

labels.name: topic:rust
labels.description: This is related to the Rust embedded library

labels.name: sdk-issue
labels.description: Issues with the Rust SDK specifically

body:
### What component does this affect?

SurrealDB Rust SDK

### Describe the bug

On `wasm32-unknown-unknown` the first access to the ML model object store panics:

panicked at surrealdb/core/src/obs/mod.rs:52:18:
current directory should be accessible

When `SURREAL_OBJECT_STORE` is unset, `obs` falls back to a default store, which is `InMemory` on wasm. Before it picks that backend, though, it resolves `env::current_dir().join(default_dir)` and runs `fs::create_dir_all` on every target, and only the native local-file-system backend uses the result. The browser has no current directory, so the `expect` panics.

The store is created lazily on first use, so this hits anything that touches model files in the browser: `Datastore::put_ml_model` (importing a model), calling `ml::<model>`, and `REMOVE MODEL`.

### Steps to reproduce

In a headless browser test (`wasm-bindgen-test`, `run_in_browser`) with `surrealdb-core` and the `kv-mem` feature:

```rust
use surrealdb_core::dbs::Session;
use surrealdb_core::kvs::Datastore;

#[wasm_bindgen_test]
async fn stores_model_files() {
      let ds = Datastore::new("memory").await.unwrap();
      let sess = Session::owner().with_ns("test").with_db("test");
      ds.put_ml_model(&sess, "model", "1.0.0", "", vec![1]).await.unwrap();
}
```

The test panics at `surrealdb/core/src/obs/mod.rs:52` instead of storing the model.

### Expected behaviour

The model file is stored in the in-memory object store the browser already falls back to. Resolving the local directory should happen only where the local file system backend uses it.

### SurrealDB version

surrealdb 3.3.0-nightly (main at 18971ffb), wasm32-unknown-unknown, Chrome headless

### Contact Details

dmitrii.a.baranov@gmail.com
